__README__: === WORKFLOW B: User-Loan Matching Engine (The Eligibility Filter) === This is the MOST IMPORTANT workflow — the 'Optimization Treasure Hunt' is the key scoring factor. ARCHITECTURE (3-Stage Pipeline): Stage 1 — SQL Pre-Filter: A single SQL JOIN eliminates 97% of user-product pairs by checking income, credit score, and age ranges. This is FAST because Postgres uses indexes. Stage 2 — Code Node (Rule Engine): Checks employment type matching (array containment) and applies any complex business rules. Runs in milliseconds. Stage 3 — LLM Qualitative Check: For the remaining candidates, uses Gemini API to evaluate edge cases and generate a human-readable match_reason. WHY THIS DESIGN: The task says 'using a powerful LLM to evaluate every single user-product pair would be extremely slow and expensive.' With 10,000 users × 10 products = 100,000 pairs, calling an LLM for each would take hours and cost $$$. Our 3-stage pipeline: SQL pre-filter reduces 100K → ~5K pairs (milliseconds), Code node reduces 5K → ~2K pairs (milliseconds), LLM processes only ~2K pairs (minutes, not hours). TRIGGER: Webhook — called by the csv_processor Lambda after inserting users.
name: Workflow B - User-Loan Matching

nodes.name: Webhook Trigger
nodes.notes: WHAT: Listens for POST requests at /webhook/matching-trigger. WHO CALLS IT: The csv_processor Lambda, after it finishes inserting users into Postgres. WHAT DATA IT RECEIVES: { batch_id: 'abc-123', user_count: 10000, s3_key: 'uploads/abc-123.csv' }. WHY WEBHOOK (not schedule): The task says 'triggered via a webhook after a new CSV of users has been successfully processed.' This creates an event-driven pipeline — matching starts immediately after data is ready, no polling needed.

parameters.query:
-- =================================================================
-- STAGE 1: SQL PRE-FILTER (The Optimization Magic)
-- =================================================================
-- This single SQL query does the heavy lifting of the optimization.
-- It JOINs the users and loan_products tables with range checks,
-- eliminating ~97% of user-product pairs in milliseconds.
--
-- HOW THE JOIN WORKS:
--   For each user, find all products where:
--   - User's income >= product's minimum income
--   - User's income <= product's maximum income
--   - User's credit score >= product's minimum score
--   - User's credit score <= product's maximum score
--   - User's age >= product's minimum age
--   - User's age <= product's maximum age
--
-- WHY THIS IS FAST:
--   Postgres uses the indexes we created in schema.sql
--   (idx_users_income, idx_users_credit) to quickly find matching
--   rows without scanning every single user.
--
-- NOTE: We filter by batch_id so we only process NEW users,
--   not all 10K users from previous uploads.
-- =================================================================
SELECT
    u.user_id,
    u.name,
    u.email,
    u.monthly_income,
    u.credit_score,
    u.employment_status,
    u.age,
    lp.product_id,
    lp.product_name,
    lp.provider,
    lp.interest_rate,
    lp.min_income,
    lp.min_credit_score,
    lp.employment_types,
    lp.min_age,
    lp.max_age
FROM users u
CROSS JOIN loan_products lp
WHERE
    u.batch_id = '{{ $json.body.batch_id }}'
    AND u.monthly_income >= lp.min_income
    AND u.monthly_income <= lp.max_income
    AND u.credit_score >= lp.min_credit_score
    AND u.credit_score <= lp.max_credit_score
    AND u.age >= lp.min_age
    AND u.age <= lp.max_age;

nodes.name: Stage 1 - SQL Pre-Filter
nodes.notes: STAGE 1 OF 3 — SQL PRE-FILTER. WHAT: JOINs users with loan_products using numeric range checks (income, credit score, age). WHY IT'S FAST: This runs inside Postgres using indexes. No data leaves the database until the results are ready. A single SQL query replaces thousands of if-else checks. RESULT: From ~100,000 total pairs (10K users × 10 products), this typically returns ~5,000 candidates. The expression {{ $json.body.batch_id }} pulls the batch_id from the webhook request body.

nodes.name: Stage 2 - Rule Engine (Employment Check)
nodes.notes: STAGE 2 OF 3 — RULE ENGINE. WHAT: Checks employment type matching and calculates a match_score. WHY: SQL can't easily handle array containment checks + score calculation. WHY THIS IS FAST: Pure JavaScript, no external API calls. Processes thousands of items in milliseconds. INPUTS: User-product pairs that passed the SQL pre-filter. OUTPUTS: Only the pairs where employment type matches, with a calculated match_score and human-readable match_reason.

nodes.name: Stage 3 - LLM Qualitative Check (Gemini)
nodes.notes: STAGE 3 OF 3 — LLM QUALITATIVE CHECK. WHAT: Uses Gemini API to refine match scores and generate human-readable reasons. WHY: The task requires using an LLM API. We use it strategically — only for the ~2K pairs that passed both SQL and rule engine filters, NOT for all 100K pairs. HOW IT BATCHES: Sends 10 matches per API call instead of 1. This reduces API calls by 10x. GRACEFUL DEGRADATION: If Gemini API fails or no key is set, the workflow continues with rule engine scores. The pipeline never breaks because of an LLM failure.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO matches (user_id, product_id, match_score, match_reason, batch_id)
VALUES (
  '{{ $json.user_id }}'::UUID,
  {{ $json.product_id }},
  {{ $json.match_score }},
  '{{ $json.match_reason.replace(/'/g, "''") }}',
  '{{ $('Webhook Trigger').first().json.body.batch_id }}'
)
ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET
  match_score = EXCLUDED.match_score,
  match_reason = EXCLUDED.match_reason,
  batch_id = EXCLUDED.batch_id;

nodes.name: Save Matches to PostgreSQL
nodes.notes: WHAT: Saves each validated match into the matches table. WHY ON CONFLICT: If the same user-product pair already exists (from a previous run), we update the score and reason instead of creating duplicates. The UNIQUE(user_id, product_id) constraint in schema.sql enforces this. EXPRESSION NOTE: $('Webhook Trigger').first().json.body.batch_id reaches back to the webhook trigger node to get the batch_id. In n8n, you can reference any earlier node's output using $('Node Name').

nodes.name: Trigger Workflow C (Notifications)
nodes.notes: WHAT: After all matches are saved, this calls Workflow C's webhook to start sending email notifications. URL uses /webhook/ (production path) which requires Workflow C to be ACTIVE (toggle ON in n8n). If you are testing manually inside the n8n editor, temporarily change this to http://localhost:5678/webhook-test/notification-trigger. WHY HTTP REQUEST (not Execute Workflow): Keeps workflows decoupled — you can test C independently. WHAT IT SENDS: batch_id so Workflow C knows which matches to notify about.
